title: the Weeping Wood Rising Anew
premise: When the border wards of Thornfell collapse and the stars vanish in a single night, August Brightwater — the last swordspeaker bound by an oath his order died keeping — discovers the wards were not broken but deliberately unmade, and that the smuggler roads he knows so well were the veins through which the poison spread. Hunted by both realms for a betrayal he did not commit, he gathers a ragged found family: a ward-scholar who lied to survive, a fugitive border-guard, and a child who hears the weeping wood itself. To end the long winter falling between the realms, August must reforge the broken covenant at the Weeping Wood's heart — a rite that demands the truth of what his order actually did, even though speaking it will cost him his oath, his name, or his life. He chooses truth: the covenant is remade not by sacrifice but by confession, and August survives, oathless but finally free, as the first stars return.
about_author: I. M. Galloway is the pen name of a former trail-crew foreman who spent a decade mapping forgotten passes in the northern ranges before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about borders, oaths, and the people who carry both too far.

chapters.title: The Night the Stars Went Out
chapters.summary: August Brightwater guides a smuggling caravan through Thornfell's high passes when the stars extinguish overhead and every border ward within fifty miles dies at once. POV: August. Emotional beat: unease hardening into dread as his oath-mark burns for the first time in fifteen years.

chapters.title: Ash on the Toll Road
chapters.summary: Descending to the border town of Harrowgate, August finds the ward-stones shattered from the inside and the garrison blaming smugglers. He saves a young ward-scholar, Wren Calloway, from a mob. POV: August. Emotional beat: reluctant responsibility; the last oath-bound man cannot walk away.

chapters.title: What Wren Knew
chapters.summary: Wren confesses she helped catalog the wards' weaknesses for the Royal Survey — work she suspects was weaponized. Her guilt mirrors August's own buried secrets. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: two liars recognizing each other, trust beginning in shared shame.

chapters.title: The Smuggler's Ledger
chapters.summary: Following his old routes, August deciphers markings showing someone used smuggler roads for months to move something toward the Weeping Wood. His former crew is implicated. POV: August. Emotional beat: betrayal — the roads he loved became the knife.

chapters.title: The Child Who Hears the Wood
chapters.summary: In a burned waystation they find Pip, an orphan who speaks in the wood's voice, reciting words of the dead covenant. The party becomes three. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: tenderness breaking through survival-hardened hearts; found family takes root.

chapters.title: Wolves of Both Realms
chapters.summary: Border-guards from both sides hunt them; August fights a former comrade, Sergeant Daine Ferro, then spares her. She defects rather than report them. POV: August. Emotional beat: loyalty tested against duty — and choosing the person over the uniform.

chapters.title: The Hollow Covenant
chapters.summary: In a ruined shrine, Wren translates Pip's fragments: the covenant binding the realms was sealed with a lie, and the wood has been weeping sap and stars ever since. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: revelation reframes everything — this was never just sabotage.

chapters.title: Old Roads, Old Debts
chapters.summary: August seeks his old mentor, Vess, who taught him the swordspeaking oaths. Vess reveals the order knew the covenant was failing and hid it. POV: August. Emotional beat: the floor drops out of his identity; his whole life served a concealment.

chapters.title: Vess's Price
chapters.summary: Vess offers August a forged covenant-scroll that could fake a renewal — survival through another lie. August refuses, and Vess sells their location to the Crown. POV: August. Emotional beat: the theme crystallized — loyalty to people over loyalty to comfortable falsehoods.

chapters.title: Flight Through the White Pass
chapters.summary: A winter storm and royal hunters force the four up the deadly White Pass. Pip channels the wood to open a path no map holds. POV: Daine. Emotional beat: the outsider guard fully joins the family; awe replacing suspicion.

chapters.title: The Court of Thorns Below
chapters.summary: Beneath Thornfell they find the hidden realm-court, starving since the wards fell, led by Lady Serevan who believes humans broke the pact. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: fear of the other dissolving into recognition of mirrored grief.

chapters.title: Swordspeaking
chapters.summary: To prove his order's good faith, August performs the full swordspeaking rite before the court, voicing every oath aloud — including the ones his masters broke. POV: August. Emotional beat: catharsis through public truth-telling; the crowd's silence becoming respect.

chapters.title: The Lie Beneath
chapters.summary: Lady Serevan reveals her side's half: the original covenant was sealed by sacrificing the wood's heart-tree, and only confessing that crime together can renew it. Neither realm wants to speak it. POV: Serevan. Emotional beat: the terrible arithmetic of survival — peace priced in humiliation.

chapters.title: Daine's Report
chapters.summary: A captured royal dispatch shows the Crown plans to burn the Weeping Wood entirely, believing it the source of the blight. POV: Daine. Emotional beat: horror at her old allegiance; the clock starts ticking.

chapters.title: The Long Winter Falls
chapters.summary: The unnatural winter reaches killing depth; refugees flood the passes. The group must choose: save refugees or race to the wood. They split the difference, sending Daine alone ahead. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: the cost of compassion measured in time they may not have.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Weeping Gate
chapters.summary: Crown soldiers and Vess's hired blades ambush the party at the wood's threshold. Vess confronts August, demanding he take the forged path. POV: August. Emotional beat: the mentor's fall complete; August mourns the man while defeating him.

chapters.title: Heartwood
chapters.summary: Inside, the dying heart-tree shows each of them their deepest truth: Wren's complicity, Daine's desertion, Pip's origin as the tree's last seed spoken human. POV: Pip. Emotional beat: terror and wonder entwined; the child learns what they are.

chapters.title: The Rite of Confession
chapters.summary: At the tree, August begins the reforging — but the rite requires both realms' representatives to confess the original sacrifice aloud. Serevan arrives wounded; the Crown army arrives armed. POV: August. Emotional beat: everything converging; truth offered with a blade at the door.

chapters.title: Stars Over Thornfell
chapters.summary: As the confessions are spoken, the first star returns — and the sight stops the army mid-march. Soldiers kneel; the commander lowers her sword. POV: Daine. Emotional beat: triumph of witness over force; the sky itself testifies.

chapters.title: What the Oath Cost
chapters.summary: The renewed covenant unbinds all swordspeaker oaths — including August's. Stripped of the mark that defined him, he faces who he is without it. POV: August. Emotional beat: grief and liberation in one breath; identity rebuilt from love instead of duty.

chapters.title: Planting the Seed
chapters.summary: Pip chooses to remain partly the tree's voice, and the family plants the new heart-seed together as spring's first thaw breaks. Serevan and the Crown sign truce terms drafted by Wren. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: quiet joy; the world made slightly more honest.

chapters.title: Roads Worth Walking
chapters.summary: One year later, August walks the passes openly as a guide, Wren and Daine rebuilding the ward-school, Pip thriving. A traveler asks if he misses his oath. He doesn't answer — he just smiles at the returning stars. POV: August. Emotional beat: resolution; survival was worth its price because he didn't pay it alone.
